item.title: Risks and resilience in the euro area financial system
item.speaker: Boris Vujčić

rating.summary: ECB Vice-President Boris Vujčić delivered a keynote on euro area financial stability risks, focusing on three main themes: AI-related vulnerabilities, sovereign debt pressures, and non-bank financial sector resilience. He noted that headline inflation has risen to 4% in October 2026 partly due to energy prices, but framed this in a financial stability rather than monetary policy context. The speech called for stronger macroprudential frameworks for non-banks rather than signaling any monetary policy direction.
rating.stance_rationale: This speech is primarily a financial stability and macroprudential address, not a monetary policy statement. While inflation figures are mentioned contextually, there is no discussion of interest rate paths, policy rate adjustments, or easing/tightening bias, making a monetary policy score inappropriate.
key_quotes: My key message today is that Europe needs more market-based finance. At the same time, however, a larger role for non-banks must go hand in hand with stronger system-wide safeguards.
Headline inflation in the euro area increased to 4% in October, from 3.8% in September, mainly due to higher energy prices.
